summary: Tesla has introduced a new, cheaper Cybertruck model in the US, priced at $59,990, making it their most affordable Cybertruck to date. The company also reduced the price of its high-end Cyberbeast model from $114,990 to $99,990. These price adjustments are part of Tesla's strategy to attract more cost-conscious buyers in 2026.

title: Tesla’s Austin robotaxis involved in 14 crashes in first 8 months
summary: Tesla's robotaxis in Austin have been involved in 14 crashes since their launch in June. These incidents include collisions with minor injuries and one with a city bus, according to federal reports.

title: Cybertruck Owner Sues Tesla for $1 Million After Autopilot Crash
summary: A Tesla Cybertruck owner is suing Tesla for over $1 million after her vehicle, using Autopilot, allegedly crashed into a concrete barrier. The lawsuit, filed in Texas, claims the vehicle nearly drove off an overpass and cites misleading self-driving advertisements and a lack of LiDAR sensors. This case adds to ongoing scrutiny of Tesla's self-driving technology and safety concerns.

title: Tesla Goes After California DMV, Suing Over False Advertising Decision
summary: Tesla is suing the California DMV after a December ruling branded the automaker a false advertiser over its "Autopilot" and "Full Self-Driving" labels. The company argues that consumers understand what the names imply and that no Tesla vehicles are fully autonomous. Tesla claims it did not receive due process and highlights its significant presence in California as a reason for the suit.

title: Stream sells Tesla-occupied facilities at Empire West Business Park in Brookshire
summary: Stream Realty Partners has sold two facilities at Empire West Business Park in Brookshire, Texas, to BGO. These facilities, totaling over 1.65 million square feet, are currently leased by Tesla, which began occupying the first building in 2022 and the second in 2025.

title: Cybercab spotted on the test track at Gigafactory Texas as production nears
summary: Tesla's Cybercab, the company's first new model since the Cybertruck, is currently being tested on the track at Gigafactory Texas. Earlier this week, workers celebrated the first Cybercab rolling off the production line. CEO Elon Musk stated that the fully autonomous robotaxi will begin limited production by April and aims to sell it for $30,000 or less.

title: Cybercab spotted on the test track at Gigafactory Texas as Tesla moves toward production
summary: Tesla's new Cybercab, expected to be the company's first new model since the Cybertruck, is currently being tested at Gigafactory Texas. While some prototypes have been seen with human drivers, the test models on the track lacked side mirrors and potentially steering wheels, aligning with CEO Elon Musk's vision for a fully autonomous vehicle. Despite Musk's promise of a $30,000 price point and limited production by April, details about its final design and application (fully autonomous robotaxi or entry-level EV with controls) remain in flux.

title: Quantum Private Wealth LLC Boosts Stake in Tesla, Inc. $TSLA
summary: Quantum Private Wealth LLC significantly increased its stake in Tesla, Inc. by 435.1% in Q3, now holding 5,335 shares valued at $2.37 million. This move comes as Tesla exceeded EPS estimates but saw a 3.1% decline in revenue year-over-year. The article highlights other institutional investors' activities, mixed analyst ratings, and recent insider selling.

title: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) DCF Valuation: Is The Stock Undervalued?
summary: This article presents a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation of Tesla, Inc. (TSLA), concluding that the stock is overvalued. Based on the analysis, Tesla's DCF value is calculated at $70.41 per share, significantly lower than its current market price of $173.74, resulting in a negative margin of safety of 146.75%. The valuation uses a 15% discount rate and 2% terminal growth rate, forecasting free cash flows from 2024 to 2028.

title: Tesla Robotaxi Crashes Raise Concerns About FSD Capabilities
summary: Investor Ross Gerber has voiced concerns regarding Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology after multiple Robotaxi crashes in Austin, Texas, suggesting that the system is not improving and may require hardware adjustments. These incidents, including a Tesla allegedly driving onto a boat ramp, raise questions about the safety and readiness of Tesla's FSD system and could impact public perception and regulatory scrutiny as the company plans to deploy a larger autonomous fleet.

title: Tesla still has to pay $243 million over fatal Autopilot crash, judge rules
summary: A federal judge has upheld a jury's verdict requiring Tesla to pay $243 million in damages related to a fatal 2019 Autopilot crash. The crash killed Naibel Benavides Leon when a Tesla driver, George McGee, ran into a parked SUV while distracted, despite trusting the Autopilot technology. The jury assigned Tesla 33% of the fault and awarded both punitive and compensatory damages.

title: Tesla canceled the car of the century
summary: Bloomberg reports on the discontinuation of Tesla's Model S and Model X, highlighting the Model S's significant impact on the automotive industry despite its upcoming phase-out. The article reminisces about the Model S's early days and its role in popularizing electric vehicles, challenging traditional sales models, and pioneering over-the-air updates, even as Tesla shifts its focus towards robots and autonomous technology.

title: Tesla unveils cheaper Cybertruck variant, cuts Cyberbeast price to drive demand
summary: Tesla has introduced a more affordable Cybertruck variant and reduced the price of its high-end Cyberbeast model, in response to challenges in attracting buyers for its electric pickup trucks. The new dual-motor all-wheel-drive Cybertruck is priced at $59,990, while the Cyberbeast's price has been cut to $99,990 from $114,990, with the "Luxe Package" likely being discontinued. These changes come as Tesla faces a slowdown in the broader EV market and aims to bolster demand for the Cybertruck.

title: Elon Musk Reiterates April Production Goal For Tesla's Cybercab, Says It Will Be 'Very Slow In The Beginning'
summary: Elon Musk has confirmed Tesla's Cybercab will begin production in April, though he anticipates a slow start due to a "radical redesign of car manufacturing." The Cybercab, lacking pedals or a steering wheel, aims for a significantly higher production rate eventually. Musk also reiterated his belief that Tesla will have the world's largest autonomous fleet in the future.
